2017_114_101717regmtg.paragraph: Agenda packet for the Troy Board of Education regular meeting of October 17, 2017 at the Services Building. Yeo & Yeo delivers an unmodified opinion on the June 30, 2017 financial statements with no material weaknesses in internal controls — but a qualified opinion on the federal Nutrition Cluster, carrying a material weakness for excess fund balance and a significant deficiency on student eligibility. The Board also commends 51 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists, approves the 2017/2018 Sex Education Advisory Board, and hears a Mission Moment on Troy High's Focus Hope program.

**Meeting**
Regular meeting, October 17, 2017, 7:00 PM, Services Building, 4420 Livernois.

**Recognition**
The Mission Moment is Troy High's **Focus Hope** program, introduced by Deputy Superintendent Mark Dziatczak with principal Remo Roncone presenting the students and staff involved.

The Board then commends **51 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists**. More than a million students from some 22,000 high schools entered nationwide and only 16,000 seniors are selected; semifinalists score in the top one and one-half percent on the PSAT with comparable SAT scores. The packet prints the roster with phonetic guides beside most names for reading aloud — "Sanjana Anil (Sun-juhn-ah A-nil)," "Himaneesh Yerrakalva (hi-MAHN YE-ruh-KAHL-vuh)," "Zeyu Yang (Bill Yang)." Copies of the resolution go to the students at a November 15 reception. Several names recur a year later among the 54 semifinalists of the following class — James Ge, Kathleen Gu, Lyndsey Gu, Claire Hao, James Li, Spencer Liu, Shankar Prabhu, Adithya Sanjay, Muyang Wang, Angela Wang, Megan Worrel and Elise Xia.

**Consent agenda**
Minutes of the September 5 special meeting and workshop, the September 19 meeting, and the August 2017 Treasurer's Report.

**Treasurer's Report — August 2017**
Total check disbursements are $8,432,205.85, the General Fund group $4,771,055.94 and the General Fund (101) itself $4,583,699.91. Adding $1,137,361.53 of wire transfers, $189,355.81 of P-Card purchases and $12,128.94 of ACH debits, less $2,938.40 of prior period voids, total disbursements in period are $9,768,113.73.

**Curriculum**
The Sex Education Advisory Board for 2017/2018 is co-chaired by **Amy Buchanan**, assistant principal at Smith, and **Nicole Jenkins**; state law requires at least half the board be parents and one parent co-chair. District personnel are Buchanan, teachers Lisa Danhoff (Troy High), Karyn Wakely (Athens) and Kevin Wilson (Boulan Park), and social worker Stacey Schoenherr (Smith); clergy is Rev. Gregg Mayberry of Big Beaver United Methodist; the health resource is David Roth of the Oakland Health Department. The following year's list is nearly identical with Kristy Pierce replacing Buchanan as the district co-chair.

**Business — the 2016-2017 audit**
David Youngstrom of Yeo & Yeo presents; a draft had gone to the Board at the October workshop.

The financial statements receive an **unmodified opinion** — the highest level of assurance — that they present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the district as of June 30, 2017.

| Fund | Fund balance, June 30, 2017 |
| --- | --- |
| General Fund | $24,205,391 |
| 2016 Capital Projects | $36,718,462 |
| Nonmajor governmental | $8,368,346 |
| **Total governmental** | **$69,292,199** |

Government-wide, total assets are $85,409,988 against total liabilities of $16,117,789, with cash and investments of $64,971,528 and $18,867,458 due from other governmental units. Revenues and other sources across all governmental funds are $212,602,835 against expenditures and other uses of $183,114,138 — a **$29,488,697 change in fund balance**, of which $36,718,462 is the newly created 2016 Capital Projects Fund and the nonmajor funds fall $9,902,871.

General Fund revenue: state $97,064,534 (67%), local $38,211,378 (26%), interdistrict sources $7,610,128 (5%), federal $3,281,077 (2%) and other $60,309. Expenditures by function: instruction $99,214,158 (69%), supporting services $43,617,694 (30%), capital outlay $619,824 (1%) and other $102,644. Instructional share has held at 68–69% across three years against an Oakland County average of 63%.

Per-pupil General Fund revenue rises from $10,641 in 2013 to $11,353 in 2017, expenses from $10,585 to $11,145. Ten-year enrollment runs 12,174, 12,177, 12,076, 12,032, 12,312, 12,438, 12,591, 12,563, 12,717 and 12,881. The **General Fund unassigned balance** moves $21,433,250, $21,000,702, $20,231,419, $21,038,513 and **$23,716,299** across 2013–2017.

**The one qualification.** Internal controls show no material weaknesses and no significant deficiencies, with management comments on federal procedures and time and effort record keeping. But on major federal programs, while the Special Education Cluster receives an unmodified opinion, the **Nutrition Cluster receives a qualified opinion**, carrying a **material weakness for excess fund balance** and a **significant deficiency for student eligibility**. Federal school-meal rules cap how much surplus a food service fund may carry; the district's food service fund balance had grown past that limit.

Future challenges named: the state economic and political condition, rising fringe benefit costs, the retirement rate increase, and **eroding state revenue sources**.

Agenda packet for the regular meeting of the Troy School District Board of Education, October 17, 2017, 7:00 PM at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. The agenda is: 1. Pledge of Allegiance; 2. Recognition — A. TSD Mission Moment: Troy High School – Focus Hope, B. 2017-18 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists; 3. Additions & Deletions; 4. Public Communication (agenda items); 5. General – Consent Agenda — A. Minutes of the September 5, 2017 Special Board of Education Meeting, B. Minutes of the September 5, 2017 Board of Education Workshop, C. Minutes of the September 19, 2017 Board of Education Meeting, D. Treasurer's Report – August 2017; 6. Personnel; 7. Curriculum — A. Consideration: Sex Education Advisory Board for 2017/2018; 8. Business — A. Report: 2016/2017 Audit, B. Consideration: 2016/2017 Audit; 9. Public Communication (non-agenda items); 10. Other; 11. Adjournment. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 19 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW) every Monday and Wednesday at 2:00 and 9:00 p.m. when school is in session, and viewable at http://vimeo.com/troyschools.

**Recognition 2.A: Troy High School Focus Hope.** Mark Dziatczak, Deputy Superintendent for Teaching and Learning, introduces the Mission Moment and invites Remo Roncone, Principal of Troy High School, to share about the school's Focus Hope program, recognizing the Troy High students and staff involved.

**Recognition 2.B: 2018 National Merit Scholarship Semifinalists.** More than one million students nationwide from some 22,000 high schools entered the National Merit Scholarship Program; only 16,000 of these seniors are selected to be semifinalists. The Board passes a resolution commending and congratulating fifty-one Troy semifinalists.

The semifinalists are Sanjana Anil, Brinda Avutapalli, Anuja Bagri, Venkatesh Bajji, Joseph Barlow, Tejas Bolar, Michelle Cai, Tuhin Chakraborty, Annie Chen, Afriti Chinoy, Liam Clancy, Emmanuel Dannug, Manasi Desai, Allen Diao, Sahil Dogra, Raul Dutta, James Ge, Kathleen Gu, Lyndsey Gu, Claire Hao, Runxuan Jiang, Yunsoo Kim, Austin Lan, James Li, Michael Lin, Spencer Liu, Kiran Menon, Anna Mitrofan, Murali Mohan, Robert Mu, Akash Nadella, Mohnish Nadella, Andrew Nguyen, Shankar Prabhu, Ashka Pujara, Adithya Sanjay, Yusuf Uzhunnan, Muyang Wang, Angela Wang, Amanda Wewer, Jonathan Wong, Megan Worrel, Elise Xia, Ashley Xu, Zeyu Yang, Himaneesh Yerrakalva, Justin Zhang, Daniel Zheng, William Zhou, Jane Zhou and Lisa Zou.

As in the following year's packet, the roster is printed with phonetic pronunciation guides beside most names so they can be read correctly from the podium — "Sanjana Anil (Sun-juhn-ah A-nil)," "Tuhin Chakraborty (Too-hin Cha-kra-boar-tee)," "Runxuan Jiang (Run-shawn Jong)," "Himaneesh Yerrakalva (hi-MAHN YE-ruh-KAHL-vuh)," "Elise Xia (Elise Shaw)," and, for one student, a preferred English name rather than a pronunciation: "Zeyu Yang (Bill Yang)."

The resolution recites that student achievement is honored through the National Merit semifinalist and finalist recognition programs, and that National Merit students reach semifinalist status by scoring in the top one and one-half percent on the National Preliminary Scholastic Aptitude Test and earning comparable scores on the Scholastic Aptitude Test. It is signed the seventeenth day of October, 2017. The item calls fifty-one a remarkable number of semifinalists and a tribute to the staff and parents of the district, and notes copies of the resolution will be presented to the students at a reception on November 15.

A dozen of these names appear again in the October 2018 packet among that year's 54 semifinalists — James Ge, Kathleen Gu, Lyndsey Gu, Claire Hao, James Li, Spencer Liu, Shankar Prabhu, Adithya Sanjay, Muyang Wang, Angela Wang, Megan Worrel and Elise Xia — and several are also among the senior scholar athletes recognized in February 2018, indicating the same cohort of students recurring across the district's recognitions.

**Consent agenda.** Minutes of the September 5, 2017 special board meeting; minutes of the September 5, 2017 board workshop; minutes of the September 19, 2017 board meeting; and the Treasurer's Report for August 2017.

**Treasurer's Report, August 2017.** General Fund (101) check disbursements are $4,583,699.91, with Total General Fund of $4,771,055.94 and TOTAL CHECK DISBURSEMENTS of $8,432,205.85. Adding ACH debits of $12,128.94, outgoing wire transfers of $1,137,361.53 and P-Card purchases of $189,355.81, and subtracting prior period void disbursements of $2,938.40, TOTAL DISBURSEMENTS IN PERIOD is $9,768,113.73. The middle sections of the packet are the August check register run by fund.

**Curriculum 7.A: Sex Education Advisory Board membership for 2017-2018.** Districts must establish a Sex Education Advisory Board; at least one-half of the board must be parents and one of the parents must co-chair. The resolution approves the membership for the 2017/2018 school year as attached.

The board is co-chaired by Amy Buchanan and Nicole Jenkins. School district personnel are Amy Buchanan, assistant principal at Smith Middle School; Lisa Danhoff, teacher at Troy High School; Karyn Wakely, teacher at Athens High School; Stacey Schoenherr, social worker at Smith Middle School; and Kevin Wilson, teacher at Boulan Park Middle School. Clergy is represented by Rev. Gregg Mayberry of Big Beaver United Methodist Church, 3753 John R Road; the health resource is David Roth of the Oakland Health Department, 1200 N. Telegraph Road, Pontiac.

Compared with the 2018-2019 roster adopted a year later, the composition is nearly unchanged — the same four district staff besides the co-chair, the same clergy member and the same health resource — with Kristy Pierce, by then assistant principal at Boulan Park, replacing Buchanan as the district co-chair alongside Jenkins.

**Business 8.A and 8.B: the 2016-2017 audit.** David R. Youngstrom, CPA, audit partner from Yeo & Yeo, presents the audit results for the year ended June 30, 2017; a draft copy of the district's audit report had been presented to the Board at the October workshop, and item 8.B asks the Board to accept the financial statements.

The opinion is unmodified — described as the highest level of assurance — meaning the district's financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Troy School District as of June 30, 2017 and the year then ended, in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.

The governmental funds balance sheet is presented across the General Fund, the 2016 Capital Projects Fund, nonmajor governmental funds and the total. Cash and investments are $18,111,636 in the General Fund, $37,164,463 in Capital Projects and $9,695,429 in nonmajor funds, totalling $64,971,528. Receivables net are $1,006,837, nil and $40,155, totalling $1,046,992. Due from other governmental units is $18,449,445, nil and $418,013, totalling $18,867,458. Prepaid items and inventory are $489,092, nil and $34,918, totalling $524,010. Total assets are $38,057,010, $37,164,463 and $10,188,515, totalling $85,409,988.

On liabilities, accounts payable and other liabilities are $3,096,925, $446,001 and $1,366,439, totalling $4,909,365. Accrued payroll and related liabilities are $10,243,243 in the General Fund alone. Unearned revenues are $511,451 and $453,730, totalling $965,181. Total liabilities are $13,851,619, $446,001 and $1,820,169, totalling $16,117,789.

Fund balance is broken out by constraint: non-spendable prepaid items and inventory $489,092 and $34,918, totalling $524,010; restricted for food service $1,116,618; restricted for debt service $2,643,654; restricted for capital projects $36,718,462 and $1,307,652, totalling $38,026,114; committed $1,090,947; assigned to capital projects $2,174,557; and unassigned $23,716,299 in the General Fund. Total fund balance is $24,205,391 in the General Fund, $36,718,462 in the 2016 Capital Projects Fund and $8,368,346 in nonmajor funds, for $69,292,199 in total.

The statement of revenues, expenditures and changes in fund balances for the year ended June 30, 2017 gives revenues and other sources of $146,227,426 in the General Fund, $40,136,105 in the 2016 Capital Projects Fund and $26,239,304 in nonmajor funds, totalling $212,602,835. Expenditures and other uses are $143,554,320, $3,417,643 and $36,142,175, totalling $183,114,138. The change in fund balance is accordingly $2,673,106, $36,718,462 and a decrease of $9,902,871, for a total increase of $29,488,697. Fund balance at July 1, 2016 was $21,532,285, nil and $18,271,217, totalling $39,803,502, rising to the $69,292,199 above.

The shape of that year is entirely the bond. The 2016 Capital Projects Fund did not exist at July 1, 2016; it took in $40,136,105 and spent $3,417,643, ending the year holding $36,718,462. The nonmajor funds fell $9,902,871 as the earlier capital program spent down. The General Fund's own operating result was a modest $2,673,106 surplus.

General Fund revenue including other sources: state $97,064,534, or 67%; local $38,211,378, or 26%; interdistrict sources $7,610,128, or 5%; federal $3,281,077, or 2%; and other $60,309, less than 1%. General Fund expenditures by object include employee benefits $45,172,027 and supplies and materials $17,726,062 at 12%, with capital outlay $619,824 and other $2,223,594. By function: instruction $99,214,158, or 69%; supporting services $43,617,694, or 30%; capital outlay $619,824, or 1%; and other $102,644, less than 1%.

The instructional expenditures comparison shows Troy at 69% for 2016-17, 69% for 2015-16 and 68% for 2014-15, against an average of all Oakland County schools of 63% for 2015-16 — the same six-point advantage the district would report the following year.

The per-pupil analysis of General Fund revenues, expenditures and transfers runs from 2013 to 2017: revenues $10,641, $10,812, $10,924, $11,094 and $11,353; expenses $10,585, $10,526, $10,560, $11,028 and $11,145. Revenue exceeds expense in every year of the series.

The ten-year enrollment trend runs 12,174 in 2008, 12,177, 12,076, 12,032, 12,312, 12,438, 12,591, 12,563, 12,717 and 12,881 in 2017 — the trough in 2011 and steady growth after.

The General Fund unassigned balance runs $21,433,250 in 2013, $21,000,702 in 2014, $20,231,419 in 2015, $21,038,513 in 2016 and $23,716,299 in 2017, the largest single-year increase of the series.

**Internal controls and compliance — the one qualification.** On internal controls the report finds no material weaknesses and no significant deficiencies, with management comments on federal procedures and on time and effort record keeping. (Both comments carry forward into the following year's audit, where time and effort record keeping is marked corrected and federal procedures remains in progress.)

On major federal programs the results diverge. The Special Education Cluster receives an unmodified opinion. The Nutrition Cluster receives a **qualified opinion**, with a **material weakness for excess fund balance** and a **significant deficiency for student eligibility**.

This is the only qualification in the report and the only one in either the 2017 or 2018 audit as carried in these packets — by the following year both federal clusters would receive unmodified opinions with no material weaknesses, no significant deficiencies and no material noncompliance. The excess fund balance finding is a specific federal constraint: school food service programs may not accumulate a surplus beyond a set limit, and the balance sheet in this same presentation shows $1,116,618 restricted for food service. The student eligibility deficiency concerns the determination of which students qualify for free and reduced-price meals. Read together with the March 2018 budget amendment, which added a $100,000 repairs and rentals line to the Food Service Fund where the original budget had none, the district's response to carrying too much food service money appears to have been to start spending it.

**Future challenges.** The auditor lists the state economic and political condition, rising fringe benefit costs, the retirement rate increase, and eroding state revenue sources. The following year's list would replace "eroding state revenue sources" with two hard numbers — a post-employment benefit obligation of nearly $77M and a net pension liability of over $225.2M.

Read as a whole, the October 2017 packet is the district's annual reckoning, and it reads well: an unmodified opinion, a clean internal control report, 69% of spending on instruction against a county average of 63%, per-pupil revenue exceeding per-pupil expense in every year of a five-year series, an unassigned balance up nearly $2.7 million, enrollment at a ten-year high, and fifty-one National Merit semifinalists. The single blemish is a federal food service program holding more money than the rules allow.
